newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - sluggish tone persists.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - sluggish tone persists.

text.p: The New York physical coffee market remained lethargic this week, as roasters continued to meet requirements on a hand-to-mouth basis, traders said.

With futures prices rebounding sharply from last week's slide to seven-week lows, and CSCE December's premium to second-month March ballooning to over 13.00 cents, processors were content to stay on the sidelines until December goes off the board next Wednesday.
"Roasters still need coffee, but don't want to pay the price," one trader said. "Nobody wants to take a position in December because of the premium."

Traders said that while prompt supplies remained tight, keeping spot differentials firm, the flow of coffee from Mexico and some Central American coffee-producing countries is expected to pick up in January.
"The tight supply situation is not going away, but it is not affecting roasters too much anymore," another trader said. "They are waiting to see what shows up in January."
Colombian coffees for prompt delivery remained especially hard-to-find -- and costly, with hefty differentials and spot parcels still priced against December.
